correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every positive-definite quadratic pullback to a scalar Euclidean form by averaging over all signed coordinate permutations, without increasing the two-sided comparison ratio. The remaining radial ratio \(F(s)=(1+\omega s^q)^{1/q}/\sqrt{1+s^2}\) has exactly one interior maximum because the sign of its logarithmic derivative is the sign of \(\omega s^{q-2}-1\). Its endpoint minimum changes exactly at \(\omega=2^{q/2}-1\), giving the stated exhaustive piecewise formula. Representative unrestricted quadratic-form numerical optimizations agreed with the formula but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The subquadratic two-dimensional Lorentz family is a standard, repeatedly studied model in Banach-space geometry, and the range \(1<q<2\) has historically required delicate exact constant calculations. The result supplies a complete exact affine-distance profile, identifies an optimal Euclidean ellipsoid, and reveals a natural phase boundary distinct from the more complicated James-constant transitions. This is a structural family theorem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or isolated numerical value.
